note: Moved from the documented confluence point (7.7533, 6.7567), which landed on a dry GloFAS grid cell (0.05 m3/s). This point was found by a small grid search around it: it returns 8629 m3/s, the right order of magnitude for combined Niger+Benue flow post-confluence. Still worth confirming against satellite imagery.
Ajaokuta town, west bank of the Niger. Draft coordinate from Wikipedia; needs river-channel confirmation.

Onyedega (Ibaji LGA HQ) is at 6.8833, 6.6833, but that cell was near-zero discharge (2.23 m3/s). Moved ~11km west by grid search to 6.8750, 6.5750, which returns 7550 m3/s — the actual Niger channel here runs further west of the town than the town-centroid coordinate suggested.
Makurdi town centre on the Benue; a known discharge measurement location (avg ~3,150 m3/s per Wikipedia).

Obagaji (Agatu LGA HQ) is at 7.8917, 7.9094, but that cell was near-zero (0.36 m3/s). Moved ~9km north by grid search to 7.9750, 7.9250, which returns 5740 m3/s and matches the Benue mainstem. Agatu is a historically flood-hit LGA, so this point matters — worth confirming against satellite imagery.

UNRESOLVED — Guma LGA centroid (Wikidata), headquartered at Gbajimba on the Benue. A grid search out to +-0.1 degrees in every direction (including diagonals) found nothing above 40 m3/s, well below mainstem Benue flows (thousands of m3/s) seen at Makurdi/Yola/Numan — either Gbajimba sits on a minor tributary rather than the mainstem, or the true channel is further away than this search radius. Needs a real GPS/satellite-imagery point before this river point is used for scoring.
Jimeta (modern Yola), on the Benue downstream of the Lagdo dam (Cameroon) — relevant to the damReleases signal.
Numan town on the Benue; a known discharge measurement location (avg ~900 m3/s per Wikipedia).
Low confidence: only a bounding box for Demsa LGA (9°25'-9°42'N, 12°08'-12°13'E) was found, this is its midpoint, not a verified town or river-channel point. Needs a real coordinate before use.
Onitsha town is at 6.1670, 6.7830 (east bank), but that cell was near-zero (7.83 m3/s). Moved ~6km west by grid search to 6.1750, 6.7250, which returns 7481 m3/s and matches the Niger mainstem.

Atani (Ogbaru LGA HQ) is at 6.1214, 6.7696 (sources also disagreed by ~0.1 deg lat, see actor/data/README.md), and that cell was near-zero (35.6 m3/s). Moved ~5km west by grid search to 6.1250, 6.7250, which returns 7481 m3/s and matches the Niger mainstem — same reading as the corrected Onitsha point just upstream, which is plausible for two towns 11km apart on the same reach.
Nzam, Anambra West LGA headquarters, near where the Anambra River meets the Niger.
Otuocha, Anambra East LGA headquarters, on the Anambra River (a Niger tributary) near Aguleri.

Ikorodu town centre is at 6.600, 3.500, but that cell was off-channel. Moved ~9km southwest by grid search to 6.5250, 3.4250, which returns 1769 m3/s — a real, substantial reading consistent with the Ogun River, which flows past Isheri (a separate, more river-adjacent community) before reaching Ikorodu and emptying into the Lagos Lagoon. Confirms Ikorodu genuinely has a riverine signal, not just urban drainage flooding — see actor/src/sources/README.md's South West expansion note.
